sections.h2: How fast can you sell a house in Brookhaven, GA?
sections.html:
Timing depends on the route: a cash sale can close on a schedule you set, while a listing runs through showings, an appraisal and a buyer's loan. The Census median value of owner-occupied homes in Brookhaven is $692,700, roughly double the $332,700 national figure, so a small percentage difference in price is a large dollar difference here.

  • Traditional listing: best exposure, but repairs, staging and lender timelines are in play.
  • For-sale-by-owner: saves a listing commission, but you manage buyers, contracts and disclosures.
  • As-is cash sale: fewer steps and no repair requests, usually at a price below a fully prepared listing.

The sections below cover what is particular to Brookhaven: how the city came to exist, what the Census says about its homes, and the permit and tax rules a seller should know before choosing.

sections.h2: What is Brookhaven, GA, and when was it founded?
sections.html:
Brookhaven is a DeKalb County city in metro Atlanta that was incorporated in December 2012, so it is one of Georgia's newest cities. Its police department started providing service on July 31, 2013. The Census Bureau lists the city at 11.69 square miles of land, with about 4,720 residents per square mile in 2020.

The city runs 19 parks, three swimming pools, two recreation centers and one community building across 352 acres of parkland, according to its Parks and Recreation page. Water and sewer service comes from DeKalb County, not from the city, and DeKalb's Department of Watershed Management handles emergencies at 770-270-6243. Local rules on short-term rentals, permits and construction hours are set by the city's own code of ordinances, so check Brookhaven's pages and not DeKalb's when you plan work on a house here.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Brookhaven homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 59,643 residents on July 1, 2025, up 5.1 percent from its April 2020 estimates base, and counts 24,271 households with 2.36 people each. Just over half of homes are owner-occupied (52.6 percent for 2020-2024), and about 71 percent of adults 25 and older hold a bachelor's degree or higher.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes, 2020-2024: $692,700.
  • Median selected monthly owner costs with a mortgage: $3,141.
  • Median gross rent: $1,882.
  • Median household income in 2024 dollars: $117,663.
  • Mean travel time to work: 25.1 minutes.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts. These are citywide medians and your own house may sit well above or below them. Foreign-born residents make up 21.1 percent of the population, and 29.2 percent of residents age 5 and older speak a language other than English at home, so buyers and tenants here come from a wide mix of backgrounds.

sections.h2: Does Brookhaven allow short-term rentals if I want to keep the house?
sections.html:
Yes, but only for owner-occupants, and only with a city permit. The City Council adopted the Short-Term Rental Ordinance on April 23, 2019, and it limits rental to 180 days per calendar year.

  • The applicant must have owned the property for more than a year and hold a current DeKalb homestead exemption.
  • A permit cannot be issued to a business entity, including an LLC, partnership or family trust.
  • An owner may hold only one permit, and permits are capped at five percent of residential parcels in each council district.
  • The one-year permit costs $25 and is renewed annually.

For anyone selling, the key rule is that a short-term rental permit expires when ownership changes. A buyer who wants to run the house as a rental has to apply for a new permit, and for pre-existing permits the city allows a new owner six months from the title transfer to apply without being refused on the district cap. Ask the city's Community Development Department how this affects your house before you advertise it to investors, because a buyer's plan to rent the house short term can depend on the permit cap in your council district.

sections.h2: What permits and work hours apply before selling a Brookhaven house?
sections.html:
Any construction or redevelopment project needs a permit from Brookhaven's Community Development Department, and the city enforces Georgia's contractor licensing rules. A homeowner can pull a permit for work on their own home with a notarized Homeowner Affidavit, but a contractor must show a state license.

The city asks you to allow 10 business days for permit review before you call to check status. Fees, including minimum fees and review fees, are listed in the city's fee schedule, and valuation is calculated from the ICC data valuation table. If you are fixing things up before listing, note the construction hours the city publishes for complaints: before 7 am or after 7 pm Monday through Friday, before 8 am or after 5 pm on Saturdays, and all day Sunday are outside the allowed window. Unpermitted work and tree removal without a permit can be reported through the city's Brookhaven Connect app, so finish permits for completed work before a buyer's inspector asks for them.

sections.h2: How do DeKalb assessments, appeals and homestead filing work for Brookhaven owners?
sections.html:
DeKalb County, not the city, assesses Brookhaven property. The County's Property Appraisal Department states that assessed value equals fair market value times 40 percent, and that you may appeal within 45 days of the notice date if you think the value, the property description or an exemption denial is wrong.

There are three appeal paths. The Board of Equalization is free and is a three-member panel; a hearing officer is available for non-homestead properties over $500,000 at no filing fee; and non-binding arbitration requires a certified appraisal at your cost plus a $217 filing fee. Online filing needs the access code from your notice, and mail appeals go to 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

Homestead timing is printed on the county's exemption page:

sections.h2: What happens to transfer tax and recording on a Brookhaven sale?
sections.html:
The deed is recorded in DeKalb County after Georgia's real estate transfer tax is paid, and the sale is reported on Form PT-61 filed electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority. The tax is based on the sale price at $1 for the first $1,000 and 10 cents per additional $100, and the Department of Revenue says it is charged to the seller unless the contract says otherwise.

For questions about whether a particular deed is exempt, the Department of Revenue directs people to the clerk of superior court in the county. The cooperative's customer support line is 800-304-5174 for filing questions. Your closing attorney will normally file the form.

faqs.a: No. Brookhaven was incorporated in December 2012 and its police department began service on July 31, 2013, so it is one of Georgia's newest cities, set inside DeKalb County.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Brookhaven, GA?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 median value of owner-occupied homes in Brookhaven is $692,700. That is a citywide median, so your own house may sit above or below it.

faqs.q: Can a new buyer keep using my house as a short-term rental?
faqs.a: Only after applying for a new permit. Brookhaven's ordinance says the permit expires on a change of ownership, and permits go only to owner-occupants who hold a DeKalb homestead exemption and have owned the property for over a year.

faqs.q: How long do Brookhaven owners have to appeal a DeKalb assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date on the assessment notice. Appeals can be filed online with the access code from the notice, or by mail to the DeKalb County Property Appraisal Department at 325 Swanton Way, Decatur, GA 30030.

faqs.q: Who pays the Georgia transfer tax when I sell in Brookhaven?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under Georgia's real estate transfer tax, though the contract can shift it to the buyer. It must be paid before the deed is recorded, and the PT-61 form is filed online.
